payload.findings_fixed:
Three findings, collected before fixing anything, then fixed in one pass.

FINDING 1 - the battery could not run at all: the worktree had no toolchain, so verify died at tsc before a single test. Root cause is the provisioning gap this iteration exists to close (se.raid-worktree-provisioning-incomplete). FIXED by c5, and the worktree now carries its own install (943ms, 3 packages).

FINDING 2 - typecheck failed on tests/kb-link.test.ts: cannot find module 'kb'. Cause: package.json declared the kb module as an npm file:-protocol dependency, and the link it created had been destroyed. FIXED by removing the declaration entirely - see finding 3 - and by retiring kb-link.test.ts, whose whole premise (that kb is importable through an npm workspace link) is now forbidden. Nothing is lost in coverage: the engine resolves imports by PATH in modules.ts and modules.test.ts already covers that.

FINDING 3 - THE INCIDENT, and the reason the design changed mid-build. A toolchain junction I created for i8c pointed at trunk's node_modules; trunk's node_modules contained kb as a symlink into the sibling benjamin checkout; a routine `git worktree remove --force` followed both links and deleted benjamin's working tree AND its .git. The owner ruled the general law: AN IMPORT IS READ-ONLY, whatever mechanism implements it - the direction of writes is the rule, not any one forbidden mechanism, deliberately generalized so a future agent cannot satisfy the letter with a new mechanism. FIXED at four levels, all mechanical rather than remembered: (a) se.law-imports-are-read-only minted in the ledger; (b) the file: dependency and the symlink it created are gone; (c) provisioning now INSTALLS the toolchain into the worktree instead of linking a shared one, so no followable path exists; (d) retirement still unlinks any legacy or hand-made link before removing a tree, because the guard that would have prevented the damage should exist regardless. Guarded by four new checks in tests/imports-readonly.test.ts - no path-protocol dependency in package.json, nothing in node_modules resolving outside the repository, no write call in the import resolver, and provisioning installing rather than linking - plus the retained safety check that a shared install survives a retirement.

DAMAGE STATUS: trunk's node_modules was emptied by the same deletion and has been reinstalled. benjamin is recoverable from its remote; the owner ruled it not a problem and deferred the re-clone. 16/16 green across the law guards and the iteration's own checks (run-3fca4e85eece).
